name: Madden Custom Offense
subtitle: Scheme Kings · Madden 27
tagline: One motion, three plays. The run keeps them honest.

answers.name: Fade Out
answers.label: The Seam Against Cover 3
answers.why: Against a single high Cover 3 we are looking for the streak on the short side of the field: it goes up the seam for a one play bomb. Make sure your fastest receiver is in the back of the stack. Because of the stack he gets a free release up the field.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak. Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post.

answers.name: Cheat Slash Wheel Cross
answers.label: The Seam Against Cover 3
answers.why: The key route is the tight end coming up the seam. Against any sort of Cover 3 single high look, the safety stays in the middle of the field, the slot fade holds the corner on the outside, and the seam just gets wide open.
answers.do: The cheat motion player starts on the wide side of the field. Middle receiver on the short side on a slot fade. Optional: the comeback on the wide side, stem it up one so it goes a little deeper.

answers.name: Mtn Seam Swirl
answers.label: The Post Over the Top
answers.why: A Cover 3 one play touchdown. The streak from the tight end holds the safety in the middle of the field, the corner route from the solo receiver pulls the corner to the outside, and the motion down post route gets up over the top, absolutely wide open.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Outside receiver on the short side on a corner route. Tight end on a streak.

answers.name: Smash Seam
answers.label: The Corner Behind the Flat
answers.why: Built to attack Cover 2. The key route is the outside release corner route, and it gets to such a tough area of the field. The flat defender sits at about fifteen yards, the streak pulls the deep defender back, and you throw it up along the sideline in behind the flat defender.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Back of the stack receiver on a streak.

answers.name: Fade Out
answers.label: The Wheel Hole Shot
answers.why: The front of the stack player on the wheel gets up in behind the flat defender. The deep defender gets held in the middle by the streak, and you can hit it as a hole shot in behind Cover 2 up along the sideline.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak. Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post.

answers.name: Mtn Choice
answers.label: Against Cover 2
answers.why: It works even better against Cover 2. Wait until the slot fade gets in behind the flat defender and drop it in along the sideline. The deep half safety has to play way more inside on the streak.
answers.do: Running back to the wide side of the field. Inside receiver on the short side on a streak. Running back on the check and release, or block him if you need more time.

answers.name: Curl Switch
answers.label: The Corner Out
answers.why: My go to man beater for this scheme. The key route is the front of the stack player on the corner out. He gets one on one, the defender is usually in an inside shade, and he breaks to the outside. If we have separation, just throw that corner out.
answers.do: Stack to the wide side of the field. Front of the stack receiver on a corner out.

answers.name: Mtn Fork Y-Corner
answers.label: The Pre-Snap Tell
answers.why: The motion gives you a tell right away that it is man. He gets up the field, breaks to the outside, and with this corner route you usually get three or four yards of separation.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field, and block him. Middle receiver on the wide side on a shallow cross. Make sure the inside receiver on the short side is on a corner route.

answers.name: Mtn Mesh
answers.label: The Corner Against Man
answers.why: Against man you get a really good pre-snap tell, because the corner follows the motion all the way across. The best option is the really quick corner route running away from all that mess in the middle of the field. One on one, he breaks to the outside, drop it in.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Solo receiver on a streak. Make sure the tight end is on a post.

answers.name: Fade Out
answers.label: Against Match: the Post
answers.why: Against match, Cover 4 quarters or Palms, put the back of the stack receiver on the post instead. The two of them interact: against quarters the wheel gets wide open, against Palms the post breaks into the middle with three, four, five yards of separation.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak. Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post.

answers.name: Mtn Mesh
answers.label: The Drag
answers.why: We are basically always looking to the short side of the field first. If people are matching the wheel up the field, the linebackers stay back under the post and the flat defender stays back under the wheel, throw that drag right away. He has so much speed coming across the field.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Solo receiver on a streak. Make sure the tight end is on a post.

answers.name: Spot Shake
answers.label: The Running Back Wheel
answers.why: Against man or match, if he goes out of the backfield and the linebackers get caught inside, throw the running back wheel quick. Or with the speed advantage on the linebacker, wait and drop it up over his head.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field. Outside receiver on a slant instead of the shake route, it happens a lot faster.

threats.name: Zero man
threats.q: How do I attack zero man?
threats.avoid: Careful out of empty: Fade Out and Curl Switch are five out, with no way of blocking a zero blitz

answers.name: Mtn Fork Y-Corner
answers.label: The Auto Motion Corner
answers.why: One of my go to man beaters. The auto motion player is the key route and one of your best players. If they are playing press, he gets off the press: he gets a free release because of the motion.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field, and block him. Middle receiver on the wide side on a shallow cross. Make sure the inside receiver on the short side is on a corner route.

answers.name: Spot Shake
answers.label: The Slant
answers.why: If everybody is playing way back under your seams with the safeties capping them, that leaves the middle of the field wide open for the slant. And against man, the slant is really our only option.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field. Outside receiver on a slant instead of the shake route, it happens a lot faster.

threats.name: Beat two safeties deep
threats.q: How do I beat two safeties deep?

answers.name: Fade Out
answers.label: The Skinny Post Against Cover 2
answers.why: Against Cover 2, the deep cross does a good job of pulling the mid read into the middle of the field. Then the skinny post on the trips side gets up over the top, inside the mid read.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak. Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post.

answers.name: Mtn Seam Swirl
answers.label: Against Cover 2
answers.why: If they do not have a mid read in the middle of the field, the corner holds the short side safety out and the other deep safety gets pulled outside. Instead of leading it over the top, lead it down the middle of the field and split the two safeties.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Outside receiver on the short side on a corner route. Tight end on a streak.

answers.name: PA Switch Verts
answers.label: The Switch Release Against Cover 2
answers.why: The switch release goes right up the seam. Against Cover 2 the guys get spread out, there is no mid read in the middle of the field, and you can drop it up over the top for about forty yards.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field. Outside receiver on the wide side on a streak, and motion him out against single high or Cover 4. Optional: running back on an option route as a checkdown.

answers.why: The key route is the outside slot fade on the short side. The streak forces the outside deep defender to come inside one or two steps to respect the seam, and that lets the slot fade get up over the top.

threats.q: How do I hit an explosive play?

answers.name: Fade Out
answers.label: Pass Lead It Up the Seam
answers.why: The safety plays more toward the far hash, because he has three vertical threats on the other side. Once he clears, pass lead it up the seam as far as you can, splitting in between the corner and the safety.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak. Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post.

answers.name: RPO Zone Peek
answers.label: He Plays the Pass: Hand It Off
answers.why: He jumps back. He is playing the pass, so hand the ball off. Because they are in pass sets they will not fly down as hard on the run, so we get to the second level and get way to the outside. Second and 20 turned into third and one.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Motion the solo receiver in, so his defender is in an outside shade and the slant comes inside.

answers.name: Bench Corner
answers.label: Eyes on the Stack
answers.why: I look to the stack side first: the little quick out and the back of the stack route. Right at the snap my eyes are on those two defenders. If they stay inside or back off, throw that little quick out route and pick up the first down.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Outside receiver on the trips side on a streak.

answers.name: Cheat Spot Y Quick
answers.label: The Flat
answers.why: The same cheat motion as Cheat Outside Zone and Cheat Slash Wheel Cross. He gets to the flat really, really quickly: if it is man he might get caught inside, if it is zone everybody drops back, and we quick throw it to the flat.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field. Outside receiver on the wide side on a slot fade. Backside receiver on a post.

answers.name: Cheat Spot Y Quick
answers.label: The Running Back Swing
answers.why: If everybody is dropping back, there is the other checkdown. The flat is open, but we also have the running back on a swing. Get it out to him and let him make a play with the ball in his hands.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field. Outside receiver on the wide side on a slot fade. Backside receiver on a post.

answers.label: Leave One Unblocked
answers.why: Trap runs have been one of the best runs in this game for a long time. You leave one of these players unblocked and let him come up the field. Your guard comes across, traps him, and you just get downhill.

answers.label: The Deep Corner
answers.why: The streak pulls the deep defender back, the flat defender has no shot, and the corner route gets so deep down the field. Save it for deep third downs where you really need to get it up over the flat defender.

about.headline: MY CUSTOM OFFENSE
copy: An offense I built from scratch in Madden 27, not copied from a real team. Four formations, the cheat motion, the empty stack shots and two man beaters I trust every snap, and every call comes out of the Seattle Seahawks playbook.

principles.title: ONE MOTION, THREE PLAYS
principles.blurb: Three plays use the same motion across the field, so it ties them together and disguises your intentions. The run, the seam and the flat all look the same.
principles.detail: The cheat motion takes the tight end across on Cheat Outside Zone, Cheat Slash Wheel Cross and Cheat Spot Y Quick, and the trips motion does the same on Mtn Same Side Zone and Mtn Mesh.

principles.title: THE RUN KEEPS THEM HONEST
principles.blurb: We are using the run to keep them honest, and every once in a while it can be explosive. The run is good, but it is really what it sets up with the next play.
principles.detail: Start with the run against a new opponent. Against zone nobody follows the motion, so the run gets an extra blocker, and when they come down to stop it the shot is behind them.

principles.title: VERTICAL PRESSURE
principles.blurb: The amount of vertical pressure you put on defenders is just absolutely ridiculous. Get a gauge on what they run, then hit the one play touchdowns.
principles.detail: Fade Out and Curl Switch out of Empty Trey Stack: the verticals shred zone and match, and the stack beats man. The shot plays bomb Cover 3 and Cover 2.

extras.text: Fade Out is the single best play I have used in Madden this year.

playbook.title: RUN THE SEAHAWKS PLAYBOOK
playbook.note: In Madden 27 this whole offense runs out of the SEATTLE SEAHAWKS playbook. Tight Y Off, Y Trips Wk, Empty Trey Stack and Tight Flex Offset all live inside it.

formations.name: Tight Y Off
formations.desc: Two receivers to one side, the tight end and a receiver to the other, and the tight end is the cheat motion. He comes across the formation on three different calls, so the outside zone, the seam behind it and the quick flat all start from the exact same look.
bullets: Nobody follows him: an extra blocker
Single high and the seam opens

show.what: Cheat Outside Zone. The tight end motions over and nobody follows him against zone. That is an extra blocker for free on the outside zone.
Cheat Slash Wheel Cross. The same motion, and against Cover 3 the tight end gets right up the seam while the slot fade holds the corner outside.
Cheat Spot Y Quick. The same motion again, and he gets to the flat really quickly. Zone drops back, quick throw it.

formations.name: Y Trips Wk
formations.desc: Trips to the wide side, and the motion comes down across the formation. The same side zone and the mesh use the same motion, so one look gives the defense two very different plays, and the seam swirl, the RPO and the red zone call live here too.
bullets: The drag beats man and zone
The post over the top of Cover 3

show.what: Mtn Same Side Zone. Nobody comes over with the motion, so he lines up in front of the back as an extra blocker on this side.
Mtn Mesh. The same motion, and the drag comes across with so much speed. Throw it right away.
Mtn Seam Swirl. The motion man gets vertical instead, and the post gets up over the top of Cover 3.

formations.name: Empty Trey Stack
formations.desc: Five out, a stack on one side and three on the other. The stack gets free releases against press and runs defenders into each other, and the vertical routes put so much pressure on the deep defenders. Our best play and our go to man beater both live here.
bullets: Fade Out shreds zone and match
Five out: nobody to block a zero blitz

show.what: Fade Out. Single high Cover 3, the streak from the back of the stack goes up the seam for a one play bomb.
Curl Switch. Out of the same look, the front of the stack gets one on one and breaks to the outside on the corner out.
Bench Corner. Eyes on the stack at the snap: they stay inside, throw the quick out and pick up the first down.

formations.name: Tight Flex Offset
formations.desc: The tight end and a flex receiver, with the back offset. The trap up the middle, the motion man beater, the play action verticals and the shots off the slot fade and the seams all come out of it.
bullets: The trap right up the A gap

show.what: 0 1 Trap. Leave one unblocked, let him come up the field, the guard traps him, and get downhill.
Mtn Fork Y-Corner. The motion gets him a free release, then he breaks to the outside on the corner.
PA Switch Verts. The switch release goes right up the seam, and against Cover 2 with no mid read you drop it over the top.

home.pitch: The offense I built from scratch in Madden 27: the cheat motion, the run that keeps them honest, Fade Out and Curl Switch out of the stack, and the shots. All of it out of the Seattle Seahawks playbook.

book.note: every formation and every call on the sheet lives inside it

plays.name: Cheat Outside Zone

reads.label: The Cheat Motion
reads.text: The great part about this play is the cheat motion we get from our tight end. He auto motions across the formation, and three plays use that same motion, so it ties them together and disguises your intentions.

reads.label: Nobody Follows Him
reads.text: If it is zone, he motions over and nobody follows him. That buys us an extra blocker for free on this side of the ball, and it helps us get a numbers advantage in the run game when we hand it off.

reads.label: Bust It to the Outside
reads.text: Hat on a hat, a double team, the tight end picking up his man and the receivers getting to the second level. You have so many blockers on this side of the ball that we bust it to the outside for about fifteen yards.

reads.label: Against Man
reads.text: You can run it versus man. It is just against zone specifically that they will not bring an extra guy over.

reads.label: Cut It Back
reads.text: If they overplay to the outside and the user and the linebackers come down super aggressively, it is a zone run, so cut it back. Put your foot in the ground and bust it right up the middle of the field.

plays.whenToUse: I always like to start with the run, and this is the first call against a new opponent. The tight end comes across, nobody follows him against zone, and that extra blocker opens the outside. Then the same motion sets up Cheat Slash Wheel Cross and Cheat Spot Y Quick.

plays.name: Cheat Slash Wheel Cross

reads.label: The Seam Against Cover 3
reads.text: The key route is the tight end coming up the seam. Against any sort of Cover 3 single high look, the safety stays in the middle of the field, the slot fade holds the corner on the outside, and the seam just gets wide open.

reads.label: Quick Throw the Wheel
reads.text: If everybody stays inside on the slot fade and the motioned over tight end up the seam, we have the wheel going up the sideline. If they have no flat defender out there, quick throw that wheel right away and get it up the sideline.

reads.label: Wait for the Wheel
reads.text: If there is a flat defender and the seam is taken away because they are in a Cover 4, wait until the wheel passes in behind the flat defender. The slot fade pulls back the deep defender, and you drop it in along the sideline.

reads.label: The Comeback Against Man
reads.text: If they run man coverage, none of the routes on the short side are really good. Our best option is the comeback as he breaks back toward the ball. Throw that comeback, catch it, get down.

reads.label: High Low the Flat Defender
reads.text: Against zone, look to the comeback or the running back in the flat and high low the flat defender. If he bites down on the running back, throw the comeback as he breaks to the ball. If he stays really far back, throw the checkdown.

adjustments: The cheat motion player starts on the wide side of the field
Middle receiver on the short side on a slot fade
Optional: the comeback on the wide side, stem it up one so it goes a little deeper
plays.whenToUse: The play off the outside zone. The same cheat motion, so it all looks the same, and against Cover 3 the tight end gets right up the seam. The wheel, the comeback and the back in the flat are there when it is not.

plays.name: Mtn Same Side Zone

reads.label: The Motion
reads.text: Another play where we are using motion coming across the field, and the same motion as Mtn Smash Choice. When we motion this guy across and it is a zone coverage, they will not bring anybody over.

reads.label: The Extra Blocker
reads.text: He lines up right in front of the running back, so when we hand the ball off we get an extra blocker right on this side. Nice blocking up front, the receivers get to the second level, cut it to the outside and get up the field for about ten yards.

reads.label: Against Man
reads.text: Against man they actually bring a guy over, which is fine. It does not cost us anything, we just do not gain an advantage, and the run is still very viable.

reads.label: Lead Us Through the Hole
reads.text: When no one comes over, he lines up right in front of the tail back, leads us right through the hole and picks up the safety.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The other run we put in, out of trips with the motion coming down. It buys an extra blocker against zone, and it is the same motion as Mtn Mesh, so the defense sees one look and gets two very different plays.

plays.name: Mtn Mesh

reads.label: The Drag
reads.text: We are basically always looking to the short side of the field first. If people are matching the wheel up the field, the linebackers stay back under the post and the flat defender stays back under the wheel, throw that drag right away. He has so much speed coming across the field.

reads.label: The Drag Against Man
reads.text: Against man, the corner has to trail him all the way across the field, and it is super hard to keep up with him. Fire it in on the run. It is a great man beater, but you have to recognize it early. You cannot throw it late.

reads.label: The Tight End Post
reads.text: If the linebacker sees that drag and leaves the middle of the field, it is the tight end post, wide open in the middle. It is almost a mesh concept without the other mesh: we are high lowing those linebackers.

reads.label: The Running Back Wheel
reads.text: Out of the backfield, if the flat defender stops his feet and does not turn and run with the wheel, the streak on this side pulls back the deep defender. Wait until the wheel crosses in behind and fire it in.

reads.label: The Corner Against Man
reads.text: Against man you get a really good pre-snap tell, because the corner follows the motion all the way across. The best option is the really quick corner route running away from all that mess in the middle of the field. One on one, he breaks to the outside, drop it in.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Solo receiver on a streak
Make sure the tight end is on a post
plays.whenToUse: One of my favorite plays in the scheme. It works versus man and it works versus zone: the auto motion drag, the tight end post behind it, the running back wheel, and the corner route against man.

plays.name: Fade Out

reads.label: The Seam Against Cover 3
reads.text: Against a single high Cover 3 we are looking for the streak on the short side of the field: it goes up the seam for a one play bomb. Make sure your fastest receiver is in the back of the stack. Because of the stack he gets a free release up the field.

reads.label: Pass Lead It Up the Seam
reads.text: The safety plays more toward the far hash, because he has three vertical threats on the other side. Once he clears, pass lead it up the seam as far as you can, splitting in between the corner and the safety.

reads.label: The Skinny Post Against Cover 2
reads.text: Against Cover 2, the deep cross does a good job of pulling the mid read into the middle of the field. Then the skinny post on the trips side gets up over the top, inside the mid read.

reads.label: The Wheel Hole Shot
reads.text: The front of the stack player on the wheel gets up in behind the flat defender. The deep defender gets held in the middle by the streak, and you can hit it as a hole shot in behind Cover 2 up along the sideline.

reads.label: No Mid Read
reads.text: If they do not keep anyone back in the middle, the deep over gets wide open, and the skinny seam is wide open too. That is a wide open touchdown.

reads.label: Against Match: the Post
reads.text: Against match, Cover 4 quarters or Palms, put the back of the stack receiver on the post instead. The two of them interact: against quarters the wheel gets wide open, against Palms the post breaks into the middle with three, four, five yards of separation.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak
Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post
plays.whenToUse: The single best play I have used in Madden this year. It beats Cover 2, Cover 3 and match for one play touchdowns, and the only thing it is not great against is man. Get a gauge on what your opponent likes to run, then bomb them.

plays.name: Curl Switch

reads.label: The Corner Out
reads.text: My go to man beater for this scheme. The key route is the front of the stack player on the corner out. He gets one on one, the defender is usually in an inside shade, and he breaks to the outside. If we have separation, just throw that corner out.

reads.label: The Z Post Against Press
reads.text: Against a press look, the back of the stack Z post does really well. The press gets all messed up because he is back and cannot really get pressed, so the defenders run into the front of the stack player and the Z post comes up clean.

reads.label: No Safety: Bomb It
reads.text: If they are in off coverage or press with no safety in the middle of the field, hold it, wait for the Z post to clear and get over the top, and bomb it deep. It is a one play touchdown possibility.

reads.label: The Shallow Cross
reads.text: Three routes on the short side of the field. I really like the shallow cross, and a lot of the time I am just going to get it out of my hands as he attacks the middle of the field. It is a really good underneath option versus man.

reads.label: The Wheel and the Dig
reads.text: If the stack is taken away and the shallow cross is too, we have the wheel breaking outside and the dig coming in over the top. Fire the dig in over the middle.

adjustments: Stack to the wide side of the field
Front of the stack receiver on a corner out
plays.whenToUse: The go to man beater. Five man beating routes on the field, and the stack brings everybody together so the defenders run into each other. Fade Out and Curl Switch out of the same look are the two plays I could run for five straight games.

plays.name: Mtn Seam Swirl

reads.label: The Post Over the Top
reads.text: A Cover 3 one play touchdown. The streak from the tight end holds the safety in the middle of the field, the corner route from the solo receiver pulls the corner to the outside, and the motion down post route gets up over the top, absolutely wide open.

reads.label: Against Cover 2
reads.text: If they do not have a mid read in the middle of the field, the corner holds the short side safety out and the other deep safety gets pulled outside. Instead of leading it over the top, lead it down the middle of the field and split the two safeties.

reads.label: The Checkdowns
reads.text: If the middle of the field is taken away, there are two checkdowns. The running back sits down against zone and breaks to the outside against man on his option route, and the return route comes into the middle of the field.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Outside receiver on the short side on a corner route
Tight end on a streak
plays.whenToUse: The motion is the exact same one as Mtn Mesh, but instead of running the mesh across the field the motion man gets vertical up over the top. Bomb Cover 3, bomb Cover 2 with no mid read, and check it down when they take the middle away.

plays.name: Spot Shake

reads.label: The Seams Against Cover 3
reads.text: The seam balls are really good against Cover 3 and really good at attacking the middle of the field. The linebacker gets pulled down by the slant as he comes across, and we have a seam on the wide side and the tight end seam.

reads.label: The Tight End Seam
reads.text: The tight end is a little slower and has to wind his way through the linebacker, so it buys you a little more time to see it. The safety bites to the wide side, so throw the tight end seam up the field.

reads.label: The Wide Side Seam
reads.text: The seam on the wide side gets down the field a lot quicker, so you have to throw it a lot quicker. The linebacker shoots in, the flat defender shoots out, the seam is open, and you have to throw it before the safety can come over.

reads.label: The Receiver Wheel Against Cover 2
reads.text: Against Cover 2, the two seams pull the deep defenders back and the receiver wheel gets outside the flat defender. If they are playing a hard flat, throw the receiver wheel as he cuts up the field.

reads.label: The Slant
reads.text: If everybody is playing way back under your seams with the safeties capping them, that leaves the middle of the field wide open for the slant. And against man, the slant is really our only option.

reads.label: The Running Back Wheel
reads.text: Against man or match, if he goes out of the backfield and the linebackers get caught inside, throw the running back wheel quick. Or with the speed advantage on the linebacker, wait and drop it up over his head.

adjustments: Running back to the short side of the field
Outside receiver on a slant instead of the shake route, it happens a lot faster
plays.whenToUse: A zone shot with two seams, two wheels and a slant over the middle. Not a great man beater: if they surprise you with man, the slant is the throw.

plays.name: Bench Corner

reads.label: Eyes on the Stack
reads.text: I look to the stack side first: the little quick out and the back of the stack route. Right at the snap my eyes are on those two defenders. If they stay inside or back off, throw that little quick out route and pick up the first down.

reads.label: Caught Inside Against Man
reads.text: Against man coverage, when they get caught inside, throw that quick out one more time, make a guy miss and turn up the sideline.

reads.label: The Shallow Seam
reads.text: If at the snap the defenders go outside underneath it, the back of the stack route goes up the seam. As long as there is no linebacker sitting in the seam, throw it up the shallow seam right when he cuts up the field.

reads.label: The Tight End Corner
reads.text: If the user jumps over and the stack side is taken away, the streak clears everyone out and we have the deep corner route from our tight end. Hit him up over the top.

reads.label: The Shallow Cross
reads.text: The fourth option. The shallow crosser can run away from his man defender, or against zone, if everyone is playing back, he is the checkdown coming across the middle of the field.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Outside receiver on the trips side on a streak
plays.whenToUse: A great quick passing concept. Read the stack side at the snap: they jump in, throw the out; they jump out, throw the shallow seam. Really good on the goal line too, especially if they play press.

plays.name: Smash Seam

reads.label: The Corner Behind the Flat
reads.text: Built to attack Cover 2. The key route is the outside release corner route, and it gets to such a tough area of the field. The flat defender sits at about fifteen yards, the streak pulls the deep defender back, and you throw it up along the sideline in behind the flat defender.

reads.label: Save It for Third and Long
reads.text: I only call this two or three times a game. I am saving it for the big third and fourth and longs where I think they will be playing deep zone drops and I have to get it in behind the flat defenders.

reads.label: The Deep Over
reads.text: If the corner route is taken away, or it looks jumbled up, there is the deep over route, the seam and the shallow in cut on the trips side. Throw the deep over as he comes over the middle of the field.

reads.label: The Shallow In Cut
reads.text: It is really a vertical concept that needs time. If they bring a big blitz and you are getting pressure, or they are playing way back and everything deep is taken away, look to the checkdown, the shallow in cut.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Back of the stack receiver on a streak
plays.whenToUse: The third and long and fourth and long call: the outside release corner gets up over the flat defenders along the sideline, with the deep over and the shallow in cut behind it.

plays.name: Post Wheel

reads.label: Quick Throw the Wheel
reads.text: Look to the trips side first with the three vertical routes. If at the snap the wheel cuts up the field and there is no flat defender, or everybody is caught inside, just quick throw it right as he cuts up the field.

reads.label: Wait for the Wheel
reads.text: If they have a flat defender, do not quick throw it. The tight end streak pulls the deep defender back, so wait until the wheel clears in behind the flat defender and drop it in.

reads.label: The Z Post
reads.text: The Z post breaks into the middle of the field, the streak pulls everyone back, and the drag and the curl hold the linebackers down. He gets so deep down the field, about 35 yards, that the linebackers never get there unless it is a user.

reads.label: The Drag and the Curl
reads.text: If both vertical options are taken, the drag is a checkdown or runs away from man coverage, and the curl sits down if the linebackers get pulled inside to take the drag.

adjustments: Trips to the short side of the field
Inside receiver on the trips side, the tight end, on a streak
plays.whenToUse: The tight end streak clears everybody out on the trips side. The wheel quick or late, the Z post deep over the middle, and the drag and the curl underneath.

plays.name: 0 1 Trap

reads.label: Leave One Unblocked
reads.text: Trap runs have been one of the best runs in this game for a long time. You leave one of these players unblocked and let him come up the field. Your guard comes across, traps him, and you just get downhill.

reads.label: No Hesitation
reads.text: We are always aiming right downhill, right away. There is no hesitation in this run.

reads.label: The Center to the Second Level
reads.text: Because we leave the defensive lineman unblocked, our center gets to the second level. The linebacker overplays to the outside, so quick hit it right downhill.

reads.label: Right Up the A Gap
reads.text: Let the defensive tackle come up the field, the linebacker overplays to the outside, and look at the hole: right up the middle of the field for fifteen, twenty yards.

plays.whenToUse: A really nice quick hitter. Leave one unblocked, the guard traps him, and hit it right up the A gap every single time.

plays.name: Mtn Fork Y-Corner

reads.label: The Auto Motion Corner
reads.text: One of my go to man beaters. The auto motion player is the key route and one of your best players. If they are playing press, he gets off the press: he gets a free release because of the motion.

reads.label: The Pre-Snap Tell
reads.text: The motion gives you a tell right away that it is man. He gets up the field, breaks to the outside, and with this corner route you usually get three or four yards of separation.

reads.label: The Post
reads.text: The post from the same side is also really good. Even with a single high safety, wait until he clears past that safety in the middle of the field and lay it in.

reads.label: The Backside Corner
reads.text: The tight end becomes the solo receiver on the backside. One on one, he breaks to the outside, another corner route.

reads.label: The Shallow Cross
reads.text: All these players come into a bunch together, which creates a lot of confusion and natural rubs, and the shallow cross comes wide open right there.

adjustments: Running back to the short side of the field, and block him
Middle receiver on the wide side on a shallow cross
Make sure the inside receiver on the short side is on a corner route
plays.whenToUse: Designed specifically to attack man coverage. The motion corner gets a free release, the post and the backside corner are one on ones down the field, and the shallow cross gets the natural rubs.

plays.name: PA Switch Verts

reads.label: The Deep Corner
reads.text: The streak pulls the deep defender back, the flat defender has no shot, and the corner route gets so deep down the field. Save it for deep third downs where you really need to get it up over the flat defender.

reads.label: Motion Him Out
reads.text: Against a single high shell or Cover 4, put the outside receiver on a streak and motion him out. If he is lined up too far inside, the streak will not pull the deep defender out.

reads.label: The Switch Release Against Cover 2
reads.text: The switch release goes right up the seam. Against Cover 2 the guys get spread out, there is no mid read in the middle of the field, and you can drop it up over the top for about forty yards.

reads.label: The Switch Release Against Cover 3
reads.text: Against Cover 3 the defenders get pulled out, we run play action, and the switch release gets right up the seam. Drop it in.

reads.label: The Option Checkdown
reads.text: If you want to push the ball and wait for the deep routes, put your running back on an option route. You have less blocking, but you have another option when the deep stuff gets taken away.

adjustments: Running back to the short side of the field
Outside receiver on the wide side on a streak, and motion him out against single high or Cover 4
Optional: running back on an option route as a checkdown
plays.whenToUse: Vertical shots off play action: the deep corner behind the streak for third and long, and the switch release up the seam against Cover 2 and Cover 3.

plays.name: Mtn Choice

reads.label: The Slot Fade
reads.text: The key route is the outside slot fade on the short side. The streak forces the outside deep defender to come inside one or two steps to respect the seam, and that lets the slot fade get up over the top.

reads.label: Pass Lead It Away
reads.text: Pass lead it up and away from the inside deep defender and bomb it up over the top of that Cover 3 defender. You need speed on the outside receiver, and you need the anticipation.

reads.label: Against Cover 2
reads.text: It works even better against Cover 2. Wait until the slot fade gets in behind the flat defender and drop it in along the sideline. The deep half safety has to play way more inside on the streak.

reads.label: The Seam
reads.text: If that defender plays step for step on the outside with the slot fade, the safety stays in the middle of the field and you can throw it up the seam instead.

reads.label: The Tight End Cross
reads.text: The tight end crosses over to the short side where the two verticals clear everybody out. If the option route pulls the flat defender down, the deep crosser comes right into that pocket.

reads.label: The Option Route
reads.text: The motioned over option route sits down against zone. If everybody is playing back or you are getting pressure, drop it down. Against man he breaks inside or out.

adjustments: Running back to the wide side of the field
Inside receiver on the short side on a streak
Running back on the check and release, or block him if you need more time
plays.whenToUse: A vertical shot against Cover 3 and Cover 2: the streak pulls the deep defender inside and the slot fade goes over the top, with the tight end cross and the option route underneath.

plays.name: RPO Zone Peek

reads.label: Read the Linebackers
reads.text: You are reading the linebackers in the middle of the field. Even against man, keep your eyes on them. If they jump down on the run, especially the backside linebacker, throw the slant. If not, just run it.

reads.label: He Plays the Pass: Hand It Off
reads.text: He jumps back. He is playing the pass, so hand the ball off. Because they are in pass sets they will not fly down as hard on the run, so we get to the second level and get way to the outside. Second and 20 turned into third and one.

reads.label: He Slow Plays It
reads.text: He is not firing down on the run, he is slow playing it. Hand the ball off, look for the hole, put your foot in the ground and turn it into seven or eight yards.

reads.label: Caught Inside: the Slant
reads.text: He backpedals, but he also gets caught inside. That is where we still have the slant as a viable option on the backside.

reads.label: The Window
reads.text: He does not totally bite on the run, but he also does not drop back on the pass. That opening is open on the backside to the slant.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Motion the solo receiver in, so his defender is in an outside shade and the slant comes inside
plays.whenToUse: A nice RPO out of this formation. Read the linebackers in the middle of the field: they jump down, throw the slant behind them; they play the pass, hand it off.

plays.name: Quick Fork Zig

reads.label: A Red Zone Beater
reads.text: A really good red zone play in this formation. This is just a great red zone play.

reads.label: Beat Man, Beat Zone
reads.text: It beats man and it beats zone. If it is a man blitz, we have to have time.

reads.label: The Outside Slant
reads.text: That outside slant is absolutely nasty. On fourth and seven we went for it with this play, and it was the touchdown.

adjustments: Trips to the short side of the field
Running back on a wheel
plays.whenToUse: The red zone beater: trips to the short side, the back on a wheel, run it into the end zone. It beats man and zone, and the outside slant is the one that scores.

plays.name: Cheat Spot Y Quick

reads.label: The Flat
reads.text: The same cheat motion as Cheat Outside Zone and Cheat Slash Wheel Cross. He gets to the flat really, really quickly: if it is man he might get caught inside, if it is zone everybody drops back, and we quick throw it to the flat.

reads.label: The Corner Route
reads.text: If the flat defenders take that away, or it is man and it is covered, look to the corner route. The slot fade pulls the defenders back and out, and you throw the corner up along the sideline as he breaks out.

reads.label: The Backside Post
reads.text: All the eye candy of the motion gets a lot of players looking at the trips side. Then the backside post comes back into the middle of the field and gets up over the linebackers.

reads.label: The Running Back Swing
reads.text: If everybody is dropping back, there is the other checkdown. The flat is open, but we also have the running back on a swing. Get it out to him and let him make a play with the ball in his hands.

adjustments: Running back to the short side of the field
Outside receiver on the wide side on a slot fade
Backside receiver on a post
plays.whenToUse: The third play off the cheat motion. The tight end gets to the flat fast, the corner and the backside post are behind it, and the back on the swing is the checkdown.
